title: Longest-living animals
measure: The oldest known age of one animal of each species, in years. Where a study gives a range, the lower end is used for ranking. Sponges and corals are left out: some may live thousands of years, but their ages are rough guesses from growth rates.

entries.name: Ocean quahog
entries.note: A clam nicknamed Ming, aged by counting the yearly growth bands in its shell. It was born in 1499.

entries.name: Greenland shark
entries.note: Radiocarbon dating in 2016 put one shark at about 392 years, somewhere between 272 and 512. The oldest known animal with a backbone.

entries.name: Bowhead whale
entries.note: The longest-living mammal, aged from proteins in its eyes.
entries.source: AnAge longevity database, via the Associated Press (2016)

entries.name: Seychelles tortoise
entries.note: Jonathan, still alive. He was fully grown, so at least 50, when he arrived on Saint Helena in 1882. The oldest known living land animal.
